questions.question: What is sleep debt?

options.text: When you do not get enough sleep
When you want to take a nap
The time you need to wake up before driving

questions.correctAnswerText: When you do not get enough sleep
questions.explanation: Sleep debt happens when you do not sleep enough. You can only pay back this debt by getting more sleep.

questions.question: Brake pads should:

options.text: Be clean and free of oil or grease

questions.correctAnswerText: Be clean and free of oil or grease
questions.explanation: When you check your brakes, make sure the pads and shoes have no oil, grease, or brake fluid on them.

questions.question: Bent lock rings:
questions.correctAnswerText: Are dangerous
questions.explanation: Bent, cracked, or mismatched lock rings are dangerous and should not be used.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a driving hazard?

options.text: A police car helping a driver on the roadside

questions.correctAnswerText: An empty, clear road
questions.explanation: Accidents can distract drivers and cause dangerous situations. Ice cream trucks attract children who may ignore traffic. Police cars on the roadside can distract drivers. An empty, clear road does not create a hazard.

questions.question: When checking the inside of a bus, you should:

options.text: Check that all seats are firmly attached
Skip checking the handrails and floor

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that all seats are firmly attached
questions.explanation: When checking the inside of a bus, make sure everything is safe and works properly. Check that all seats are securely fastened so passengers can use them safely.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you must show all of the following about oil EXCEPT:

options.text: That the oil level is safe
That the oil level is above the refill mark
That the oil level is below the refill mark

questions.correctAnswerText: That the oil level is below the refill mark
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must show where the dipstick is, that the oil level is safe, and that the oil level is above the refill mark. You should NOT show that it is below the refill mark.

questions.question: Cargo in a trailer:

options.text: Does not need to be tied down
Should be stacked no higher than three feet
Must be secured to prevent shifting
Should have heavy items on top of light items

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be secured to prevent shifting
questions.explanation: Cargo must be secured so it does not move while the vehicle is in transit. Load cargo to keep the vehicle balanced and stable.

questions.question: A driver should always:

options.text: Drive faster than the speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan for emergencies
questions.explanation: While driving, watch the road ahead for hazards. Plan what you will do if a hazard becomes dangerous.

questions.question: Driving at night is:

options.text: Safer than driving during the day
Just as safe as driving during the day
More dangerous than driving during the day

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous than driving during the day
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous than day driving. It is harder to see, headlight glare can hurt your vision, and more tired and impaired drivers are on the road.

questions.question: With a manual transmission, you can stop the vehicle from rolling backward by:

options.text: Slightly releasing the clutch before lifting your foot off the brake
Putting the vehicle in reverse before moving forward
Fully releasing the clutch before lifting your foot off the brake
Putting the vehicle in neutral before moving forward

questions.correctAnswerText: Slightly releasing the clutch before lifting your foot off the brake
questions.explanation: To prevent rolling backward when starting on a hill, slightly release the clutch before lifting your foot off the brake. Use the parking brake if needed to keep the vehicle from rolling.

questions.question: When parked on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Use only the rear flashing lights.
Use one set of turn signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: Turn on your four-way emergency flashers when you park on the side of the road. This is very important at night.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: You should move your vehicle quickly.
You should move your vehicle slowly.
The move should be made with a jerking motion.
You do not need to use a turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should move your vehicle slowly.
questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and smoothly. This keeps your vehicle under control and gives other drivers time to see you and move. Always use your turn signal.

questions.question: If a tire fails, you should:

options.text: Wave your arms at other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: Using the brakes after a tire fails can cause you to lose control. Unless you are about to hit something, stay off the brakes until your vehicle slows down.

questions.question: When checking under your vehicle for leaks, you should look for all of the following except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Windshield wiper fluid.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, look under your vehicle for leaks of oil, coolant, grease, or fuel.

questions.question: When going downhill, how can you need less braking?
questions.correctAnswerText: Switch to a lower gear.
questions.explanation: Shift to a lower gear before going downhill. This helps your vehicle stay at a safe speed without using the brakes too much.

questions.question: About how many drinks does it take for a 200-pound person to reach a 0.02 percent blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects you before you reach the legal limit. A 200-pound person reaches a BAC of 0.02 percent after one drink.

questions.question: Shaded areas of the road:

options.text: Usually do not contain moisture, so they can't freeze.
Will remain slick after ice on other areas of the road has melted.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will remain slick after ice on other areas of the road has melted.
questions.explanation: Shaded areas get less sunlight and stay cooler longer. Ice in these areas stays longer than on sunny spots. They can be icy and slippery even after other areas have melted.

questions.question: If driving in fog, you should not:
questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your speed.
questions.explanation: If you must drive in fog, slow down. Use your low beam headlights and fog lights. Turn on your four-way flashers. Never speed up in fog.

questions.question: When putting out an electrical fire:

options.text: Use a B or C extinguisher.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a B or C extinguisher.
questions.explanation: B and C type fire extinguishers work on electrical fires. Never use water on an electrical fire because it can cause electric shock.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Allow the rear wheels to lock up
Allow all wheels to lock up
Alert other motorists when you are braking

questions.correctAnswerText: Help prevent wheel lockup
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on a slippery surface.
